### Steps to reproduce issue

 Please see toy example here: https://gitlab.com/cclaunch/bad_parameter_repro.git .  I get the same results in humble, jazzy, and rolling.
 
1. Form a `SetParameters` request
2. Fill in an invalid parameter type ID (something greater than 9 currently), e.g. `10`
3. Send the request
4. The receiving end node will crash with a `std::runtime_error` `Unknown type: 10`

### Expected behavior

The node with the parameter being set should not crash.

### Actual behavior

The node with the parameter being set crashes with `std::runtime_error` `Unknown type: <invalid_type_id>`

### Additional information

We noticed this issue because we have some UI code in javascript that interfaces to several services we proxy to our robot.  It was a miss on our part to add to the enumeration of types incorrectly (which brought us to 10, which was invalid), but still I would not expect an invalid parameter type in a request from a remote client to crash the entire parameter server side process.  In this particular case the node in question was also part of a larger component container and the entire container crashes.  I think the recommendation that makes sense here is for the set parameters call to fail at the client end.

Steps to reproduce issue

Please see toy example here: https://gitlab.com/cclaunch/bad_parameter_repro.git . I get the same results in humble, jazzy, and rolling.

  1. Form a SetParameters request
  2. Fill in an invalid parameter type ID (something greater than 9 currently), e.g. 10
  3. Send the request
  4. The receiving end node will crash with a std::runtime_error Unknown type: 10

Expected behavior

The node with the parameter being set should not crash.

Actual behavior

The node with the parameter being set crashes with std::runtime_error Unknown type: <invalid_type_id>

Additional information

We noticed this issue because we have some UI code in javascript that interfaces to several services we proxy to our robot. It was a miss on our part to add to the enumeration of types incorrectly (which brought us to 10, which was invalid), but still I would not expect an invalid parameter type in a request from a remote client to crash the entire parameter server side process. In this particular case the node in question was also part of a larger component container and the entire container crashes. I think the recommendation that makes sense here is for the set parameters call to fail at the client end.
